A penetrating shell, or any kinetic / high-explosive shell landing where the armor is already below armorMinFraction, can set off the ammunition of a ballistic or missile weapon near where it went in (within 50 / 70 / 100 units for small / medium / large mounts, times cookoffReachMult).
Energy weapons have no magazine to go up, but the same kind of hit can wreck one for good (until a tender repairs it), with no blast or fire.
A magazine cook-off may start a fire where it went up; a shell that breaches the hull may start a smaller one, less often.

Radar missiles flown by vanilla's guided-missile AI (pure pursuit, which ends up tail-chasing and looping on long flights) get TCO's lead guidance instead: they steer for where the target will be.
Radar missiles are never launched at small craft (fighters, drones, shuttles), unless the launcher is anti-fighter or point defence.
your side's autofiring radar launchers fire at radar tracks beyond sight (the game's AI only sees what is in sight)
Radar scope, bottom right, while you pilot a ship: north up, out to the ship's radar range against a capital, with the returns its radar (or datalink) holds.

ECM Package: jams ecm<Size> incoming radar missiles at a time (homing on the ship, or on a friend within ecmRange) within ecmRange, costing ecmPowerPerMissile of the reactor's capacity per second each.
Noise jamming (ECM Package): a cloud of radar noise jamRadius<Size> around the ship.
Nebula clouds weaken radar: the signal x nebulaSignalMult for each of the radar, the midpoint and the target that is inside a cloud.
Radar missiles on TCO's lead guidance steer around asteroids.
Every guided missile launcher, from any mod, is sorted into IR or radar guidance.

IR lock: every ship has a heat signature, 0-1: 0.1 for the hull, up to 0.5 more for running engines (all working and thrusting; idle engines count 60%%, damaged ones less, flamed out none; seen from behind x1.3, from the front x0.75), up to 0.5 more for flux (venting = full).

Every ship carries flares by hull size (more with the Expanded Countermeasures Dispenser: ecdFrigateMult on frigates, ecdOtherMult on the rest) and drops a salvo of flareSalvo<Size> at a time, at most every flareCooldown seconds.

IRCCM hullmod: IR missiles fired by the ship (or its fighters) never lose a cold target by themselves, and each flare decoys them with irccmChanceCold x (1 - targetHeat)^2, plus irccmBlanketPerFlare for every enemy flare past irccmBlanketStart burning within irccmBlanketRadius of the missile (at most irccmChanceMax).
Ships with a flare-launcher ship system (vanilla or modded: any system whose weapon fires flares) get flareReloads full reloads of their flares instead.
In RTS mode the map outside what your side's ships can see is covered by a dark shadow, and enemy ships in it are hidden (you can't select or order attacks on them).
Also while piloting a ship or on normal controls (no shading there): enemy ships and their reticles beyond what your side can see are hidden.
